content_groups.group_title: Q1. What is the purpose of symphysis-fundal height?

blocks.text: To provide a simple clinical assessment of uterine/fetal growth during pregnancy and identify pregnancies requiring further assessment.

content_groups.group_title: Q2. What can cause a large fundal height?

blocks.text: Multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, macrosomia, fibroids and incorrect dating, among other causes.

content_groups.group_title: Q3. What can cause a small fundal height?

blocks.text: FGR, oligohydramnios, incorrect dating, fetal malpresentation/engagement and other uterine or maternal factors.

content_groups.group_title: Q10. What are the main causes of FGR?

blocks.text: Maternal disease, placental insufficiency and fetal causes such as chromosomal abnormalities, infection and structural/genetic abnormalities.

content_groups.group_title: Q11. What is the definitive treatment for severe placental FGR?

blocks.text: There is no medication that reverses established placental insufficiency; management involves appropriate surveillance and delivery at the safest time.

content_groups.group_title: Q12. Does FGR automatically require caesarean section?

blocks.text: No. Mode of delivery depends on fetal condition, gestational age, Doppler/CTG findings and other obstetric factors.

"A 32-week woman has an EFW on the 5th centile. What do you do?"
"An EFW on the 5th centile indicates that the fetus is small for gestational age, but this does not by itself establish fetal growth restriction."

"I would review the previous growth measurements and assess the growth trajectory. I would also assess the abdominal circumference, amniotic fluid volume and umbilical artery Doppler, with additional Doppler studies where indicated."

"I would assess the mother for hypertension and evidence of pre-eclampsia and review the fetal movements. Depending on the gestational age and clinical findings, I would arrange appropriate fetal surveillance, including CTG where indicated."

"If there were evidence of significant growth restriction, abnormal Dopplers, maternal disease or fetal compromise, I would involve the specialist obstetric/fetal medicine team and plan delivery according to the balance between the risks of prematurity and continuing the pregnancy."
